blocks.text: Dohra:

(Dear readers) listen to the account of chivalrous feats of the Khalsa, How their miniscule minority conquered the Mughals in majority. Included among these chosen ones was the (Author's) grandfather, Who had taken a vow to sacrifice his life for his religion. (1)
lines: (Dear readers) listen to the account of chivalrous feats of the Khalsa,
How their miniscule minority conquered the Mughals in majority.
Included among these chosen ones was the (Author's) grandfather,
Who had taken a vow to sacrifice his life for his religion.

blocks.text: It was Nawab Khan Bahadur4 (Zakariya Khan) of Lahore, Who had suppressed the Khasa Panth very much. Calling an assembly of all the representatives of the state, He had issued such a written proclamation at Lahore: (20
Chaupai:

That whosoever provided a shelter to the Singhs, He would have to forego his own precious life. Whosoever did not inform about the Singh's approach, He would also have to be divested of his existence. (3)
lines: That whosoever provided a shelter to the Singhs,
He would have to forego his own precious life.
Whosoever did not inform about the Singh's approach,
He would also have to be divested of his existence.

blocks.text: Whosoever established a relationship of blood with the Singhs, He would have to accept conversion to Islam. Whosoever handed over provisions to the Singhs, He would be converted to Islam for this offence. (4)
lines: Whosoever established a relationship of blood with the Singhs,
He would have to accept conversion to Islam.
Whosoever handed over provisions to the Singhs,
He would be converted to Islam for this offence.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Holding out such threats and stringent admonitions, He created a scarce among the general populace. Conferring robes of honour on some of the people, He created sharp divisions within the Community. (5)
lines: Holding out such threats and stringent admonitions,
He created a scarce among the general populace.
Conferring robes of honour on some of the people,
He created sharp divisions within the Community.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

After this, people started supplying information about Singhs, Some of them even getting the Singhs arrested themselves. Many among them started killing Singhs directly, So miserable became the plight of Singhs (in Punjab). (5)
lines: After this, people started supplying information about Singhs,
Some of them even getting the Singhs arrested themselves.
Many among them started killing Singhs directly,
So miserable became the plight of Singhs (in Punjab).

blocks.text: Presenting Singhs' bodies before the Mughals after killing them, They used to get rewarded with gold coins for their deeds. Since a confrontation developed between the people and the Singhs, The Singhs also started hitting back in retaliation. (7)
lines: Presenting Singhs' bodies before the Mughals after killing them,
They used to get rewarded with gold coins for their deeds.
Since a confrontation developed between the people and the Singhs,
The Singhs also started hitting back in retaliation.

blocks.text: Since the Singhs would take a refuge somewhere after hit and run, The wicked opponents would soon complain to the Mughals. Hearing the complaint, the Mughals would soon raid the place, Razing the whole village, sheltering the Singhs, to ashes. (8)
lines: Since the Singhs would take a refuge somewhere after hit and run,
The wicked opponents would soon complain to the Mughals.
Hearing the complaint, the Mughals would soon raid the place,
Razing the whole village, sheltering the Singhs, to ashes.

blocks.text: If the Singhs took refuge in the wilds, leaving the sheltering villagers, The Mughal troops would start ruining the surrounding villages. At this, getting desperate at such a devastation, The Singhs abandoned the idea or taking refuge in their own country. (9)
lines: If the Singhs took refuge in the wilds, leaving the sheltering villagers,
The Mughal troops would start ruining the surrounding villages.
At this, getting desperate at such a devastation,
The Singhs abandoned the idea or taking refuge in their own country.

blocks.text: So, while some of the Singhs took refuge in the wilds in the South, Some others took refuge in the eastern mountains. Those who remained within the territory of their own state, Felt as scared as the quails in the presence of hawks. (10)
lines: So, while some of the Singhs took refuge in the wilds in the South,
Some others took refuge in the eastern mountains.
Those who remained within the territory of their own state,
Felt as scared as the quails in the presence of hawks.

blocks.text: Dohra:

My grandfather, leaving the territory of his own state, He reached the city of Jaipur in the State of Rajasthan. After arranging a meeting with the state chief, He managed to get employment in the state service. (11)
lines: My grandfather, leaving the territory of his own state,
He reached the city of Jaipur in the State of Rajasthan.
After arranging a meeting with the state chief,
He managed to get employment in the state service.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As more Singhs reached Jaipur after hearing of Mehtab Singh's employment, Mehtab Singh expressed his concern for his motherland. He enquired about the latest news from his homeland, And the areas which the Mughal troops had occupied. (12)
lines: As more Singhs reached Jaipur after hearing of Mehtab Singh's employment,
Mehtab Singh expressed his concern for his motherland.
He enquired about the latest news from his homeland,
And the areas which the Mughal troops had occupied.

blocks.text: The Singhs replied that it was difficult to describe, The atrocities that the Mughals had committed there. Neither could their tongue dare to utter those brutalities, Nor would his ears be able to listen to those. (13)
lines: The Singhs replied that it was difficult to describe,
The atrocities that the Mughals had committed there.
Neither could their tongue dare to utter those brutalities,
Nor would his ears be able to listen to those.

blocks.text: Neither could their lungs dare to describe those indignities, Nor could their hearts contain those in silence. Being caught between the devil and the deep sea, They could neither retaliate, nor bear with those indignities. (14)
lines: Neither could their lungs dare to describe those indignities,
Nor could their hearts contain those in silence.
Being caught between the devil and the deep sea,
They could neither retaliate, nor bear with those indignities.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The Mughals had committed the greatest sacrilege, In the sacred precincts of Darbar Sahib at Amritsar. The chief among the Mughals had kept a Courtesan, (For lewd dancing) in the sanctum sanctorum of Harmandir. (15)
lines: The Mughals had committed the greatest sacrilege,
In the sacred precincts of Darbar Sahib at Amritsar.
The chief among the Mughals had kept a Courtesan,
(For lewd dancing) in the sanctum sanctorum of Harmandir.

blocks.text: This Mughal chief hailedfrom village Mandiali, And Massa Ranghar was the name of this chief. Being a great sinner and a notorious evil doer, He had been desecrating the sanctity of Harmandir. (16)
lines: This Mughal chief hailedfrom village Mandiali,
And Massa Ranghar was the name of this chief.
Being a great sinner and a notorious evil doer,
He had been desecrating the sanctity of Harmandir.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Hearing of this desecration, Mehtab Singh felt greatly incensed, As if he had been stung by a poisonous scorpion. He asked if there were no Singhs present there, Who could crush the head of such a defiler? (17)
lines: Hearing of this desecration,
Mehtab Singh felt greatly incensed,
As if he had been stung by a poisonous scorpion.
He asked if there were no Singhs present there,
Who could crush the head of such a defiler?

blocks.text: Had the Singhs abandoned their mission to defend the truth, Or Had they abandoned their mission of performing noble deeds? Counter-questioning him for his flamboyant bravado, Singhs asked, Why did he himself shirk from that daring challenge? (18)
lines: Had the Singhs abandoned their mission to defend the truth,
Or Had they abandoned their mission of performing noble deeds?
Counter-questioning him for his flamboyant bravado,
Singhs asked,
Why did he himself shirk from that daring challenge?

blocks.text: As he himself had fled away for saving his own life, How could he blame others for not facing the challenge? As he had saved his life by fleeing from the scene, So had others fled away following his footsteps. (19)
lines: As he himself had fled away for saving his own life,
How could he blame others for not facing the challenge?
As he had saved his life by fleeing from the scene,
So had others fled away following his footsteps.

blocks.text: Since all the Singhs had run away to save their lives, Hardly any Singh could be found there in Punjab. Since no body had heard of Singhs being there, People were poking fun at the so-called Singhs. (20)
lines: Since all the Singhs had run away to save their lives,
Hardly any Singh could be found there in Punjab.
Since no body had heard of Singhs being there,
People were poking fun at the so-called Singhs.

blocks.text: Since the Mughal Nawab had totally eliminated the Khalsa Panth, No Singh was supposed to be alive in the whole country. All those Singhs had perished who used to wage a war daily, As well as those Khalsa Singhs who used to meditate on God's name. (21)
lines: Since the Mughal Nawab had totally eliminated the Khalsa Panth,
No Singh was supposed to be alive in the whole country.
All those Singhs had perished who used to wage a war daily,
As well as those Khalsa Singhs who used to meditate on God's name.

blocks.text: All those Singhs had become extinct who used to recite gurbani, As well as those who used to loot and slaughter the Mughals. There were no more such Singhs as observed the daily Sikh code of conduct,
Nor were there any Singhs who sacrificed their lives with the shouts of Akal. Only the likes of him, the fugitive Singhs, had been left behind, Who had hastily escaped to save their skins. (22)
lines: Nor were there any Singhs who sacrificed their lives with the shouts of Akal.
Only the likes of him, the fugitive Singhs, had been left behind,
Who had hastily escaped to save their skins.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Hearing this, S. Mehtab Singh felt so much mortified, As if he had been stung by a poisonous scorpion. So much mortified did he feel by these remarks, That he resolved to sacrifice his life without any fear. (23)
lines: Hearing this,
S.
Mehtab Singh felt so much mortified,
As if he had been stung by a poisonous scorpion.
So much mortified did he feel by these remarks,
That he resolved to sacrifice his life without any fear.

blocks.text: Sortha:
There was one Sukha Singh of village Mari Kamboki, Who belonged to the community of carpenters. He volunteered to accompany Mehtab Singh, As he too was a devout Sikh of the Guru. (24)
lines: There was one Sukha Singh of village Mari Kamboki,
Who belonged to the community of carpenters.
He volunteered to accompany Mehtab Singh,
As he too was a devout Sikh of the Guru.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Both these Singhs bade farewell to the Singhs with Fateh, After seeking their permission for their mission with reverence. They declared their resolve to decimate the Mughals, And thereafter touch the sacred feet of Khalsa Panth. (25)
lines: Both these Singhs bade farewell to the Singhs with Fateh,
After seeking their permission for their mission with reverence.
They declared their resolve to decimate the Mughals,
And thereafter touch the sacred feet of Khalsa Panth.

blocks.text: If they sacrificed their lives for the Guru's cause, They would feel blessed both in life and death. Curse be on the mother and the father of a Singh, Who felt scared of fighting against the Mughals. (26)
lines: If they sacrificed their lives for the Guru's cause,
They would feel blessed both in life and death.
Curse be on the mother and the father of a Singh,
Who felt scared of fighting against the Mughals.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Why should a Singh be scared of death, Who had partaken Khande-ki-Pahul5 ? A Singh was as fearless as the wife of a slain Rajput warrior, Who made an offering of Sindhur6 as a vow to die with her husband. (27)
lines: Why should a Singh be scared of death,
Who had partaken Khande-ki-Pahul5 ?
A Singh was as fearless as the wife of a slain Rajput warrior,
Who made an offering of Sindhur6 as a vow to die with her husband.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Covering the distance in stages, the two Singhs reached their homeland, But they could not enter the periphery of Amritsar. Devising a strategy to accomplish their cherished mission, They decided to disguise themselves as revenue collecting officials. (28)
lines: Covering the distance in stages, the two Singhs reached their homeland,
But they could not enter the periphery of Amritsar.
Devising a strategy to accomplish their cherished mission,
They decided to disguise themselves as revenue collecting officials.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The two Sikhs invoked the protection of the God Almighty, As they planned to hit their coveted target after reaching there. They prayed that they might succeed in beheading Massa Ranghar, That there be no impediments to block their way. (29)
lines: The two Sikhs invoked the protection of the God Almighty,
As they planned to hit their coveted target after reaching there.
They prayed that they might succeed in beheading Massa Ranghar,
That there be no impediments to block their way.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The Divine Satguru, creating favourable circumstances for them, Made them to undertake their mission in the peak hours of the noon. They wrapped their faces with a loose garment, As one protected one's face during a dust storm. (30)
lines: The Divine Satguru, creating favourable circumstances for them,
Made them to undertake their mission in the peak hours of the noon.
They wrapped their faces with a loose garment,
As one protected one's face during a dust storm.

blocks.text: Dohra:

It being the peak hour of the noon in the month of September, The Sun was at its hottest in this (humid) month. As it rained and stopped at intermittent intervals, It proved very convenient for accomplishing their mission. (31)
lines: It being the peak hour of the noon in the month of September,
The Sun was at its hottest in this (humid) month.
As it rained and stopped at intermittent intervals,
It proved very convenient for accomplishing their mission.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As the scorching heat made the guards recede into shade, The rest of the troops receded to their barracks to escape rain. Massa Ranghar ordered the Court dancer to play Rag Sarang7 , Along with the melodies from the Rag Malhar.8 (32)
lines: As the scorching heat made the guards recede into shade,
The rest of the troops receded to their barracks to escape rain.
Massa Ranghar ordered the Court dancer to play Rag Sarang7 ,
Along with the melodies from the Rag Malhar.8

blocks.text: Dohra:

With some of the guards dozing off or half-asleep, None of them could notice the entry of the Singhs. The two Singhs were able to reach the main entrance, Without any let or hindrance on their way. (33)
lines: With some of the guards dozing off or half-asleep,
None of them could notice the entry of the Singhs.
The two Singhs were able to reach the main entrance,
Without any let or hindrance on their way.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Positioning their horses on each side of the main entrance, They concealed their spears behind the wall. They hid their swords beneath their loose robes, So that no security guard could object to their arms. (34)
lines: Positioning their horses on each side of the main entrance,
They concealed their spears behind the wall.
They hid their swords beneath their loose robes,
So that no security guard could object to their arms.

blocks.text: Some security guards took them for Mughal soldiers, Who had come to deposit revenue proceeds. While some guards were distracted by the live music, Others were hypnotized by the courtesan's lewd dance. (35)
lines: Some security guards took them for Mughal soldiers,
Who had come to deposit revenue proceeds.
While some guards were distracted by the live music,
Others were hypnotized by the courtesan's lewd dance.

blocks.text: As the Singhs thought this moment to be most opportune, They proceeded hastily towards their cherished target. As Divine Will wished to set everything right, It made their presence unnoticed by the watching eyes. (36)
lines: As the Singhs thought this moment to be most opportune,
They proceeded hastily towards their cherished target.
As Divine Will wished to set everything right,
It made their presence unnoticed by the watching eyes.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Both the Singhs finally reached the central spot, Where the musicians were playing on the music. Pulling out his sword from its sheath beneath his dress, Mehtab Singh lunged it courageously at Mass Ranghar's head. (37)
lines: Both the Singhs finally reached the central spot,
Where the musicians were playing on the music.
Pulling out his sword from its sheath beneath his dress,
Mehtab Singh lunged it courageously at Mass Ranghar's head.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
He chopped off Massa Ranghar's head as easily, As one plucks a pumpkin from a creeper. Whatever jewels Massa Ranghar was wearing around his neck, The other Singh took these off his neck quickly. (38)
lines: He chopped off Massa Ranghar's head as easily,
As one plucks a pumpkin from a creeper.
Whatever jewels Massa Ranghar was wearing around his neck,
The other Singh took these off his neck quickly.

blocks.text: As there was raised a lot of hue and cry all around, The two Singhs mounted their horses and fled away. As the two Singhs, spurring their horses, disappeared into the wilds, Their brave act ended the (notorious) tale of Massa Ranghar. (39)
lines: As there was raised a lot of hue and cry all around,
The two Singhs mounted their horses and fled away.
As the two Singhs, spurring their horses, disappeared into the wilds,
Their brave act ended the (notorious) tale of Massa Ranghar.

blocks.text: As the din and noise continued for a long time, It could be heard for long at the peak of noon. As they had never apprehended any sudden attack, They had no worries about Massa Ranghar's security. (40)
lines: As the din and noise continued for a long time,
It could be heard for long at the peak of noon.
As they had never apprehended any sudden attack,
They had no worries about Massa Ranghar's security.

blocks.text: Although a large number of Mughal troops were stationed there, They remained careless and involved in festivities. Feeling drowsy and sleepy in the summer noon's heat, They were overpowered by slumber at that moment. (41)
lines: Although a large number of Mughal troops were stationed there,
They remained careless and involved in festivities.
Feeling drowsy and sleepy in the summer noon's heat,
They were overpowered by slumber at that moment.

blocks.text: Dohra:

By the time, the Mughal soldiers mounted their horses, The Singhs had gone too far to be caught by them. Learning that their main custodian had been killed, They could do nothing but grieve over their loss. (42)
lines: By the time, the Mughal soldiers mounted their horses,
The Singhs had gone too far to be caught by them.
Learning that their main custodian had been killed,
They could do nothing but grieve over their loss.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As there was a joy and victory in the Singh's camp, There was a lot of sorrow and grief in the enemy camp. Then the grieving members of the family of Massa Ranghar, Proceeded to Lahore to appeal for a relief. (43)
lines: As there was a joy and victory in the Singh's camp,
There was a lot of sorrow and grief in the enemy camp.
Then the grieving members of the family of Massa Ranghar,
Proceeded to Lahore to appeal for a relief.

blocks.text: Demanding the arrest of the slaughterers of their chief, They pressed for cutting their bodies into pieces. Otherwise, they would approach the Nawab at Delhi, And complain that Lahore Nawab had lost his grip over the state. (44)
lines: Demanding the arrest of the slaughterers of their chief,
They pressed for cutting their bodies into pieces.
Otherwise, they would approach the Nawab at Delhi,
And complain that Lahore Nawab had lost his grip over the state.

blocks.text: So the Nawab came to know about this news, That the Singhs had killed Massa Ranghar. Swooping like a hawk from the skies on Massa Ranghar, The Singhs had disappeared unnoticed by anybody. (45)
lines: So the Nawab came to know about this news,
That the Singhs had killed Massa Ranghar.
Swooping like a hawk from the skies on Massa Ranghar,
The Singhs had disappeared unnoticed by anybody.

blocks.text: Neither did anybody know where those Singhs lived, Nor did anybody know where they had disappeared. Hearing this news, the Nawab felt as desperate as, A fish felt when thrown out of water. (46)
lines: Neither did anybody know where those Singhs lived,
Nor did anybody know where they had disappeared.
Hearing this news, the Nawab felt as desperate as,
A fish felt when thrown out of water.

blocks.text: He ordered all those subjects to be summoned, Who had given written undertakings to be loyal subjects. He summoned all those on the pay rolls of the state, So that he could replace them from their appointed posts. (47)
lines: He ordered all those subjects to be summoned,
Who had given written undertakings to be loyal subjects.
He summoned all those on the pay rolls of the state,
So that he could replace them from their appointed posts.

blocks.text: He ordered Niranjania Harbhagat9 to be summoned, Along with Karama Chhina10 from the village Chhina. Orders were issued to summon Rama Randhawa11, As well as Dharam Dass from Jodh Nagar12 . (48)
lines: He ordered Niranjania Harbhagat9 to be summoned,
Along with Karama Chhina10 from the village Chhina.
Orders were issued to summon Rama Randhawa11,
As well as Dharam Dass from Jodh Nagar12 .

blocks.text: The Majithias came voluntarily without being summoned, Who had been harassing the Singhs quite a lot. It is difficult to keep a count of all the informers, I (the author) have listed only his nearest neighbours. (49)
lines: The Majithias came voluntarily without being summoned,
Who had been harassing the Singhs quite a lot.
It is difficult to keep a count of all the informers,
I (the author) have listed only his nearest neighbours.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Summoning all the Hindu Jat informers of the region, Nawab of Lahore ordered them to produce the killer Singhs. They must hand them over to the authorities at any cost, Those Singhs who had slaughtered Massa Ranghar. (50)
lines: Summoning all the Hindu Jat informers of the region,
Nawab of Lahore ordered them to produce the killer Singhs.
They must hand them over to the authorities at any cost,
Those Singhs who had slaughtered Massa Ranghar.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Otherwise, the Nawab threatened to include them among the Singhs, And would eliminate them as well along with the Singhs. Since they had taken the responsibility for Singhs' elimination, They had been boasting of having eliminated the Singhs completely. (51)
lines: Otherwise, the Nawab threatened to include them among the Singhs,
And would eliminate them as well along with the Singhs.
Since they had taken the responsibility for Singhs' elimination,
They had been boasting of having eliminated the Singhs completely.

blocks.text: They must reveal the hide-outs where Singhs took shelter, So that he might raze the whole habitat to dust. They must name the town where the Singhs took refuge, So that he might massacre all the inhabitants without any delay. (52)
lines: They must reveal the hide-outs where Singhs took shelter,
So that he might raze the whole habitat to dust.
They must name the town where the Singhs took refuge,
So that he might massacre all the inhabitants without any delay.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Whosoever would supply any information about the Singhs, Along with their names, hideouts and village names, Or whosoever would facilitate the capture of any Singh, He would be highly rewarded for his services. (53)
lines: Whosoever would supply any information about the Singhs,
Along with their names, hideouts and village names,
Or whosoever would facilitate the capture of any Singh,
He would be highly rewarded for his services.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Harbhagat, a follower of Niranjani sect, informed, That it was the handiwork of one Mehtab Singh Bhangoo. He had been reported to be a resident of Mirankot, A village situated at a distance of three miles from Amritsar. (54)
lines: Harbhagat, a follower of Niranjani sect, informed,
That it was the handiwork of one Mehtab Singh Bhangoo.
He had been reported to be a resident of Mirankot,
A village situated at a distance of three miles from Amritsar.

blocks.text: Mir Kambar Ali had been given the custodianship of that village, By virtue of his being the spiritual guide of the emperor. So the Nawab, sending for the Sayyad Kambar Ali, Asked him to accompany the Mughal troops to his village. (55)
lines: Mir Kambar Ali had been given the custodianship of that village,
By virtue of his being the spiritual guide of the emperor.
So the Nawab, sending for the Sayyad Kambar Ali,
Asked him to accompany the Mughal troops to his village.

blocks.text: The Nawab had not massacred the village population for Pir's sake, Although he had not desisted from harbouring the Singhs. (56)
lines: The Nawab had not massacred the village population for Pir's sake,
Although he had not desisted from harbouring the Singhs.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The Mughal troops laid a siege to the village after reaching there, Rendering Sayyad (Kambar Ali) helpless from protecting his village. One Natha Khehra13 being the elected village chief, Was taken into custody by the invading Mughal troops. (57)
lines: The Mughal troops laid a siege to the village after reaching there,
Rendering Sayyad (Kambar Ali) helpless from protecting his village.
One Natha Khehra13 being the elected village chief,
Was taken into custody by the invading Mughal troops.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Noordin, who was a commander of the Mughal force, Addressed Natha Khehra, in the following words. He would have to wash his hands off his own life, Otherwise he must produce Mehtab Singh before him. (58)
lines: Noordin, who was a commander of the Mughal force,
Addressed Natha Khehra, in the following words.
He would have to wash his hands off his own life,
Otherwise he must produce Mehtab Singh before him.

blocks.text: Mehtab Singh must be handed over to the authorities, Otherwise his harbourers would not be spared. Thereupon, Natha Khehra answered the Mughal commander, That Mehtab Singh was not present in the village at that moment. (59)
lines: Mehtab Singh must be handed over to the authorities,
Otherwise his harbourers would not be spared.
Thereupon,
Natha Khehra answered the Mughal commander,
That Mehtab Singh was not present in the village at that moment.

blocks.text: Offering himself for arrest to the chief of Mughal troops, He asked them to deal with him in any manner they liked. At this, Noorudin ordered him to produce Mehtab Singh's son, In case he wished his own life to be spared. (60)
lines: Offering himself for arrest to the chief of Mughal troops,
He asked them to deal with him in any manner they liked.
At this,
Noorudin ordered him to produce Mehtab Singh's son,
In case he wished his own life to be spared.

blocks.text: Natha Khehra argued that he would trace Mehtab Singh's son, Provided they promised to spare the child's life. Noorudin retorted that he would not be spared. Because how could a murderer Singhs' progeny be allowed to live? (61)
lines: Natha Khehra argued that he would trace Mehtab Singh's son,
Provided they promised to spare the child's life.
Noorudin retorted that he would not be spared.
Because how could a murderer Singhs' progeny be allowed to live?

blocks.text: Hearing this decision, Natha Khehra went to the child, And shook his head out of pity for the infant. He commiserated that incase he handed over the child, They would slaughter the child in an instant. (62)
lines: Hearing this decision,
Natha Khehra went to the child,
And shook his head out of pity for the infant.
He commiserated that incase he handed over the child,
They would slaughter the child in an instant.

blocks.text: Dohra:

In case, he handed over the child to be Mughals, He would lose his face among the village elders. When Mehtab Singh demanded his son back left in his custody, He would feel stigmatized for breach of trust in heavens. (63)
lines: In case, he handed over the child to be Mughals,
He would lose his face among the village elders.
When Mehtab Singh demanded his son back left in his custody,
He would feel stigmatized for breach of trust in heavens.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

After reflecting thus, Natha Khehra declared thus, That he would die with the child rather than handing him over. If his own progeny survived after his death for the cause, They would earn the honour of being descendents of a benefactor. (64)
lines: After reflecting thus,
Natha Khehra declared thus,
That he would die with the child rather than handing him over.
If his own progeny survived after his death for the cause,
They would earn the honour of being descendents of a benefactor.

blocks.text: Dohra:

So picking up the child of Mehtab Singh on his back, Naatha Khehra jumped over the wall in the back yard. Escorting the child under the protection of five men, They escaped towards a path leading to village Mari Kamboki. (65)
lines: So picking up the child of Mehtab Singh on his back,
Naatha Khehra jumped over the wall in the back yard.
Escorting the child under the protection of five men,
They escaped towards a path leading to village Mari Kamboki.

blocks.text: The escorting party included his real son and his sister's son, As well as the family security guard and a menial. It being the peak of a hot summer's noon, They covered a lot of distance in the open fields. (66)
lines: The escorting party included his real son and his sister's son,
As well as the family security guard and a menial.
It being the peak of a hot summer's noon,
They covered a lot of distance in the open fields.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

HarbhagatNiranjania, having received the information, Heard that Natha Khehra had escaped over the back walls. Informing the Mughal troops about the escape, He himself rushed to guide the Mughal troops. (67)
lines: HarbhagatNiranjania, having received the information,
Heard that Natha Khehra had escaped over the back walls.
Informing the Mughal troops about the escape,
He himself rushed to guide the Mughal troops.

blocks.text: He felt he would be disgraced if they escaped, So they must rush and kill the fugitives. Hearing this, the Mughal troops launched an attack, After tracing the footsteps of the runaway fugitives. (68)
lines: He felt he would be disgraced if they escaped,
So they must rush and kill the fugitives.
Hearing this, the Mughal troops launched an attack,
After tracing the footsteps of the runaway fugitives.

blocks.text: Dohra:

At this juncture, Nantha Khehra, addressing his companions, Asked them to listen to his instructions carefully. He instructed them to run away with the child Rai Singh (Mehtab Singh's son), While he would try to obstruct the chasing Mughal troops. (69)
lines: At this juncture,
Nantha Khehra, addressing his companions,
Asked them to listen to his instructions carefully.
He instructed them to run away with the child Rai Singh (Mehtab Singh's son),
While he would try to obstruct the chasing Mughal troops.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Addressing his own son, he asked him to runaway, While carrying the infant Rai Singh on his shoulders. If he abandoned the child at this critical hour, He would have to face social condemnation of the society. (70)
lines: Addressing his own son, he asked him to runaway,
While carrying the infant Rai Singh on his shoulders.
If he abandoned the child at this critical hour,
He would have to face social condemnation of the society.

blocks.text: In that case, people would accuse them of abandoning the child, For whom they had deserted their own home and hearth. Therefore, while he (Natha Khehra) would grapple with the chasing troops, They (Natha's son and child) should run and seek shelter in some village. (71)
lines: In that case, people would accuse them of abandoning the child,
For whom they had deserted their own home and hearth.
Therefore, while he (Natha Khehra) would grapple with the chasing troops,
They (Natha's son and child) should run and seek shelter in some village.

blocks.text: Once the child Rai Singh14 was given a safe sanctuary, Let any catastrophe strike Natha Khehra's own son. Since Rai Singh's father had left his son in his custody, He was prepared to face death for keeping his trust. (72)
lines: Once the child Rai Singh14 was given a safe sanctuary,
Let any catastrophe strike Natha Khehra's own son.
Since Rai Singh's father had left his son in his custody,
He was prepared to face death for keeping his trust.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Upon this, Natha Khehra's son told his father, That it would not avail them to run away at that stage. Since death was hovering over their heads all around, It would no longer avail them to seek a shelter. (73)
lines: Upon this,
Natha Khehra's son told his father,
That it would not avail them to run away at that stage.
Since death was hovering over their heads all around,
It would no longer avail them to seek a shelter.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

By this time, they were surrounded by the Mughal troops, Who opened a barrage of bullet fire on them. At this, Natha Khehra's party rushed back with a counter attack, And pushed the invading troops away from their proximity. (74)
lines: By this time, they were surrounded by the Mughal troops,
Who opened a barrage of bullet fire on them.
At this,
Natha Khehra's party rushed back with a counter attack,
And pushed the invading troops away from their proximity.

blocks.text: Dohra:

At this, the Mughal Commanders issued fresh instructions, That let the supporters of Massa Ranghar be summoned forth. Addressing the brothers of Massa Ranghar, Mughal Commander said, That they should now fight and take revenge from their enemies. (75)
lines: At this, the Mughal Commanders issued fresh instructions,
That let the supporters of Massa Ranghar be summoned forth.
Addressing the brothers of Massa Ranghar,
Mughal Commander said,
That they should now fight and take revenge from their enemies.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

At this, the supporters of Massa Ranghar attacked Natha Khehra's party, While firing from a safe distance from all sides. The Natha Khehra's Jat group could not combat the enemy, As it had no firearms in their possession. (76)
lines: At this, the supporters of Massa Ranghar attacked Natha Khehra's party,
While firing from a safe distance from all sides.
The Natha Khehra's Jat group could not combat the enemy,
As it had no firearms in their possession.

blocks.text: As two of them had only spears in their hands, They kept on piercing the chests of Ranghar adversaries, The heavy club that the menial carried in his hand, He struck its heavy blow on the head of Massa Ranghar's brother. (77)
lines: As two of them had only spears in their hands,
They kept on piercing the chests of Ranghar adversaries,
The heavy club that the menial carried in his hand,
He struck its heavy blow on the head of Massa Ranghar's brother.

blocks.text: The sword that the security guard was wielding, He wounded many horse-mounted Mughal soldiers with it. After this, the Ranghar brothers fled and reported to the Mughals, That they could not fight to eliminate the Jats. (78)
lines: The sword that the security guard was wielding,
He wounded many horse-mounted Mughal soldiers with it.
After this, the Ranghar brothers fled and reported to the Mughals,
That they could not fight to eliminate the Jats.

blocks.text: They told that each arrow shot by Natha Khehra Jat, Pierced through the body which it struck. The Mughals countered since they were Massa Ranghar's brothers, They themselves should settle their scores with their enemies. (79)
lines: They told that each arrow shot by Natha Khehra Jat,
Pierced through the body which it struck.
The Mughals countered since they were Massa Ranghar's brothers,
They themselves should settle their scores with their enemies.

blocks.text: Since the Ranghar brothers were also paid Mughal soldiers, Why should they look for help to the Mughal troops? They should approach Harbhagat Niranjania's contingent, And launch a combined attack from the two sides. (80)
lines: Since the Ranghar brothers were also paid Mughal soldiers,
Why should they look for help to the Mughal troops?
They should approach Harbhagat Niranjania's contingent,
And launch a combined attack from the two sides.

blocks.text: Hearing this, Harbhagat Niranjania also expressed his inability, That his contingent would also fail to kill Natha Khehra's party. He remarked that whosoever got struck with Natha Khehra's arrow, Could not survive his deadly arrow's blow. (81)
lines: Hearing this,
Harbhagat Niranjania also expressed his inability,
That his contingent would also fail to kill Natha Khehra's party.
He remarked that whosoever got struck with Natha Khehra's arrow,
Could not survive his deadly arrow's blow.

blocks.text: Neither could they be killed with weapons or horse's hooves, Nor with the bullets packed with the sharp splinters. Natha Khehra who was renowned as an ace shooter, He could shoot his arrows as far as Ram Tirath15 . (82)
lines: Neither could they be killed with weapons or horse's hooves,
Nor with the bullets packed with the sharp splinters.
Natha Khehra who was renowned as an ace shooter,
He could shoot his arrows as far as Ram Tirath15 .

blocks.text: Dohra:

So, as instructed by the pleas of Harbhagat Niranjania, The Mughal troops made a rush from all the sides. Thus surrounding Natha Khehra's party from all sides, They launched an attack from the two sides. (83)
lines: So, as instructed by the pleas of Harbhagat Niranjania,
The Mughal troops made a rush from all the sides.
Thus surrounding Natha Khehra's party from all sides,
They launched an attack from the two sides.

blocks.text: At this, Natha Khehra realized it in his own mind, That they could not escape death at any cost now. Now when the final moment could not be put off any longer, They should do or die whatever the consequences. (84)
lines: At this,
Natha Khehra realized it in his own mind,
That they could not escape death at any cost now.
Now when the final moment could not be put off any longer,
They should do or die whatever the consequences.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Now such was the velocity of an arrow shot by Natha Khehra, That it pierced through the enemy's body and crossed over. But then as ill luck would have it or God willed it so, That Natha Khetra's bow got unhooked from its string. (85)
lines: Now such was the velocity of an arrow shot by Natha Khehra,
That it pierced through the enemy's body and crossed over.
But then as ill luck would have it or God willed it so,
That Natha Khetra's bow got unhooked from its string.

blocks.text: After that, dashing his bow to the ground in disgust, He took out his sword and started wielding it. Whomsoever he struck after making a strong dash, He fell flat on to the ground with its fatal blow. (86)
lines: After that, dashing his bow to the ground in disgust,
He took out his sword and started wielding it.
Whomsoever he struck after making a strong dash,
He fell flat on to the ground with its fatal blow.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As the Mughal soldiers were armed with muskets, They fired shots at Natha Khehra's group from a distance. But Natha Khehra's party had only hand held weapons, They could not hit the Mughal troops at a distance. (87)
lines: As the Mughal soldiers were armed with muskets,
They fired shots at Natha Khehra's group from a distance.
But Natha Khehra's party had only hand held weapons,
They could not hit the Mughal troops at a distance.

blocks.text: So the Mughal troops killed them with the gunshots, And crushed them under the horses hooves. So in this encounter, one of the survivors was Natha Khehra's sister's son, While the other survivor happened to be infant Rai Singh. (88)
lines: So the Mughal troops killed them with the gunshots,
And crushed them under the horses hooves.
So in this encounter, one of the survivors was Natha Khehra's sister's son,
While the other survivor happened to be infant Rai Singh.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Now the focus shifts to the author's father (Rai Singh), And the way he survived in this fierce encounter. As everyone pounced upon Natha Khehra from all sides, They raised a lot of noise while firing from their guns. (89)
lines: Now the focus shifts to the author's father (Rai Singh),
And the way he survived in this fierce encounter.
As everyone pounced upon Natha Khehra from all sides,
They raised a lot of noise while firing from their guns.

blocks.text: The innocent child tried to cling to Natha Khehra's feet, Who was being attacked with weapons from all sides. As Natha Khehra ran back and forth while fighting, The helpless child could not keep pace with his protector. (90)
lines: The innocent child tried to cling to Natha Khehra's feet,
Who was being attacked with weapons from all sides.
As Natha Khehra ran back and forth while fighting,
The helpless child could not keep pace with his protector.

blocks.text: As the child fell down crushed by Natha Khehra's feet, He could not run fast enough to reach him again. Feeling extremely scared of the gunshots being fired, The child tried to take cover under the thorny bushes. (91)
lines: As the child fell down crushed by Natha Khehra's feet,
He could not run fast enough to reach him again.
Feeling extremely scared of the gunshots being fired,
The child tried to take cover under the thorny bushes.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As the soldiers tried to crush the child with horses' hooves, The child tried to catch hold of the horses legs. As he struggled to rise, run and find a cover, There seemed no possibility of his remaining alive. (92)
lines: As the soldiers tried to crush the child with horses' hooves,
The child tried to catch hold of the horses legs.
As he struggled to rise, run and find a cover,
There seemed no possibility of his remaining alive.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
As the child was being tossed, tumbled and harassed, The child was desperately trying to save his life. As he was tumbled over by the horses' kicks, He was hit by a sword's blow on his neck. (93)
lines: As the child was being tossed, tumbled and harassed,
The child was desperately trying to save his life.
As he was tumbled over by the horses' kicks,
He was hit by a sword's blow on his neck.

blocks.text: His neck being slit but his Adam's Apple still intact, Another attempt was made to slit his throat as well. As his collarbone got slashed upto his shoulder, A third attempt was made to chop off his head. (94)
lines: His neck being slit but his Adam's Apple still intact,
Another attempt was made to slit his throat as well.
As his collarbone got slashed upto his shoulder,
A third attempt was made to chop off his head.

blocks.text: As the sword, cutting through his shoulder, struck into the earth, His jugular vein got spared by this stroke. The soldiers thought that the child had died by then, As his body was lying flat covered in dust. (95)
lines: As the sword, cutting through his shoulder, struck into the earth,
His jugular vein got spared by this stroke.
The soldiers thought that the child had died by then,
As his body was lying flat covered in dust.

blocks.text: Dohra:

They left after meting out such fatal blows, And taking the child to be dead after such brutality. A female vegetable vender, after having sold her stuff, Happened to reach the spot where the child lay. (96)
lines: They left after meting out such fatal blows,
And taking the child to be dead after such brutality.
A female vegetable vender, after having sold her stuff,
Happened to reach the spot where the child lay.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Spotting out the child to be alive and still breathing, She brought the child home in her vegetable basket. Knowing that the author's father's had another aunt, She brought the fatally wounded child to village Rudiala.16 (97)
lines: Spotting out the child to be alive and still breathing,
She brought the child home in her vegetable basket.
Knowing that the author's father's had another aunt,
She brought the fatally wounded child to village Rudiala.16

blocks.text: As a village cobbler sewed up his gaping wounds, The author's father was lucky to have survived. This was how the incidents of this episode proceeded, And I (the author) have completed it with God's grace. (98)
lines: As a village cobbler sewed up his gaping wounds,
The author's father was lucky to have survived.
This was how the incidents of this episode proceeded,
And I (the author) have completed it with God's grace.
